problem: Existing LLM-ROS integrations expose robot functions but leave navigation data such as occupancy grids as raw numeric arrays that LLMs cannot use for spatial or semantic goal reasoning. Adding LLM capabilities also usually needs custom robot-specific wrappers.
motivation: Non-expert users should be able to command robots in natural language, which requires LLMs to reason over maps and semantics without re-engineering the ROS stack. The observation is that rendering occupancy grids as metric, pose-aware images and storing waypoint-level semantic records lets any MCP-compatible LLM reason about goals through standardized tools.
key_idea: Expose a navigation-oriented representation layer (metric annotated map images plus waypoint-level semantic records) as reusable MCP tools so an LLM can pick exploration and navigation goals on top of an unmodified ROS SLAM/Nav2 stack.
insight: Converting occupancy grids into images with axes, grid and robot pose lets the LLM do spatial reasoning (unexplored regions, room sizes) with no dedicated reasoning module. Semantic recording at waypoints gives 100% success on the object query, but this is under complete annotations and only to waypoint-level anchors. Task 2 failures (misreading a corridor as a room, wrong room size estimates) and the difference between backends (86.67% vs 93.33%) show that performance depends on the quality of the spatial representation and on the backend's capability. There is no ablation against raw-grid text input.
method: subscribe_map_as_image: reshapes an OccupancyGrid into a 2D grayscale image (unknown=127, free=255, occupied=255(1-g/100)) and flips it vertically to match the image frame
draw_map_axis: overlays coordinate axes and an adaptive metric grid (spacing from N≈15 divisions, rounded to intuitive values), using the world-to-image transform from resolution and origin
draw_robot_pose: draws the current (x,y,θ) robot pose as an arrow marker on the map image

Semantic annotation (write_semantic_data / get_semantic_data): stores per-waypoint YAML records {name, description, pose, safety landmarks, functional landmarks, geometric features}, filtered by a prompt-defined policy; the LLM retrieves the most relevant waypoint and uses its pose as an approximate goal
MCP integration: tools are Python functions decorated with @mcp.tool(), built on ROS-MCP Server for generic topic/service/action access; the LLM issues Nav2 goals with Cartographer SLAM unchanged
Exploration prompt: a predefined prompt makes the LLM choose a waypoint at least 5 m away toward the largest unexplored area, navigate, record semantics, and repeat until 90% coverage

setting.backbone: Claude Sonnet 4.6 and GPT-5.5 (frozen, via MCP)

setting.action_space: LLM-selected map-frame goal poses (x, y, yaw) executed by Nav2

setting.privileged: none (ground-truth map is used only for coverage evaluation)

numbers_note: Only a small custom simulated scene was evaluated; no standard benchmark and no baseline comparisons.
results: Both backends reach over 97% map coverage (Claude Sonnet 4.6 97.83%, GPT-5.5 99.78%). They achieve 86.67% and 93.33% success on the smallest-room task, and 100% on the semantic object task. There are no baselines, so no comparison is reported.
limitations: Evaluated only in one small simulated warehouse with two rooms, no real robot, no baselines and no ablation against raw-grid or text input
Semantic navigation gets waypoint-level approximate goals and assumes complete, clean annotations; the 100% success is in this favorable setup
Spatial reasoning fails on ambiguous structures (corridor mistaken for room, wrong room-size estimates) and depends on the backend
